reforms.description: The fiscal year 1966 budget introduced a significant increase in general account budget spending, marking a shift in fiscal policy to stimulate economic recovery. Additionally, the Financial Loan and Investment Programme (FLIP) was expanded by 25% over the initial 1965 programme to enhance public investment.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The increase in budget spending and expansion of public investment are aimed at stimulating economic recovery, which supports growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Both reforms were part of the fiscal year 1966 budget and are stated to be implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms represent a significant structural change in fiscal policy aimed at economic recovery.
reforms.source_quote: The most important features of the new programme were: i) a 17.9 per cent increase of initial general account budget spending over the initial 1965 budget.
